journal.text: Initial deployment: invest $49,000 equally across seven high-relative-strength names and retain $1,000 cash. NVDA and AVGO provide liquid AI/semiconductor leadership; STX and LITE add strong storage/networking momentum; DASH, AXON, and NFLX diversify the trend portfolio across delivery, public-safety technology, and media. All seven were near recent highs as of 2025-06-30, with positive intermediate and short-term price trends. Equal notionals cap each initial position near 14% and avoid share-order gap failures. Reconsider or trim a holding if it closes below its recent 10-session support, develops a sustained lower-high/lower-low pattern, or materially lags the stronger eligible names; add cash or rotate rather than average down.

journal.text: Hold all seven positions. The 2025-07-01 pullback in NVDA, AVGO, LITE, DASH, AXON, and NFLX was sharp but did not produce a closing break below each name's recent 10-session support; STX instead advanced to a new 30-session closing high. Intermediate trends remain positive, and rotating immediately after one adverse session would overreact to normal momentum volatility. Keep the $1,000 cash reserve. Reconsider on a close below recent support—approximately NVDA 142, AVGO 246, STX 131, LITE 86.5, DASH 219, AXON 770, or NFLX 1215—or if relative strength deteriorates over multiple sessions rather than just one day.

Hold all positions and the $1,000 cash reserve. Through 2025-07-02, NVDA and AVGO rebounded from the prior session, while STX extended to another 40-session closing high on increased volume. DASH stabilized and remains above its recent breakout area. LITE and NFLX weakened modestly but remain above the stated support levels. AXON is the closest risk: its 774.55 close barely held the approximately 770 exit threshold after testing 756.72 intraday, so it warrants tight monitoring but not a premature sale under the close-based rule. Reconsider AXON on a close below 770; otherwise retain the prior support triggers of roughly NVDA 142, AVGO 246, STX 131, LITE 86.5, DASH 219, and NFLX 1215, or rotate if multi-session relative weakness develops.

Hold all seven positions and the $1,000 cash reserve. Through 2025-07-03, NVDA and AVGO completed strong two-session rebounds to near their recent highs, STX remained near its breakout high after only a modest pullback, and AXON rebounded decisively from its support test to 795.48. LITE also recovered, while DASH and NFLX consolidated above their breakout/support zones. None triggered the established close-based exits, and the intermediate uptrends remain intact, so trading after normal short-term volatility is unwarranted. Reconsider on closes below roughly NVDA 142, AVGO 246, STX 131, LITE 86.5, DASH 219, AXON 770, or NFLX 1215, or on sustained relative weakness over several sessions.

Hold all seven positions and the $1,000 cash reserve. Through 2025-07-07, NVDA and AVGO remain near recent highs, STX is still holding its late-June/early-July breakout, and DASH rebounded strongly to 246.89. AXON extended its recovery to 802.16 after the early-July support test. LITE and NFLX remain the softer holdings, but their closes of 91.08 and 1289.62 are still above the established close-based risk levels and their intermediate trends have not broken. The broader screen offers strong alternatives such as DDOG, but its recent gap makes chasing with the small reserve less attractive than maintaining disciplined exposure. Reconsider on closes below roughly NVDA 142, AVGO 246, STX 131, LITE 86.5, DASH 219, AXON 770, or NFLX 1215, or if several sessions of relative weakness justify rotation.

Hold all seven positions and the $1,000 cash reserve. Through 2025-07-08, NVDA advanced to 160 and remains the clearest leader. AVGO is consolidating near its highs, while DASH and LITE remain above their late-June breakout/support areas. STX pulled back to 144.47 for a third session after its sharp breakout, but it still holds the prior breakout region and does not yet justify selling. AXON's volatile 790.22 close and NFLX's 1275.31 close remain above the established close-based risk levels, though both warrant monitoring. No exit threshold was triggered, so avoid reacting to one soft session across several holdings. Reconsider on closes below roughly NVDA 142, AVGO 246, STX 138, LITE 86.5, DASH 219, AXON 770, or NFLX 1215; also reconsider STX or NFLX if relative weakness persists for several sessions.

Hold all seven positions and the $1,000 cash reserve. Through 2025-07-09, NVDA broke to a fresh 162.88 high on stronger volume, AVGO rebounded to 277.90 near its highs, and DASH, AXON, and NFLX all finished higher. STX remains the main risk: its fourth consecutive decline to 142.01 came on increased volume, but it is still above the roughly 138 breakout/risk area, so selling before the established close-based trigger would be premature. LITE at 90.44 also remains above support. The broader leadership remains constructive, but deploying the small reserve after fresh highs offers less benefit than retaining flexibility. Reconsider on closes below roughly NVDA 151, AVGO 262, STX 138, LITE 86.5, DASH 232, AXON 770, or NFLX 1215; rotate STX sooner if it closes below 138 or fails to stabilize over the next few sessions.

Exit AXON and rotate $6,000 into SNPS, retaining the balance as cash. AXON closed at 732.99 after a high-volume 9% decline, decisively breaching the previously established 770 close-based risk level and erasing its early-July recovery; discipline outweighs waiting for a rebound. SNPS closed at 566.19 on increased volume, a fresh 60-session high after clearing its early-July 555 area, providing stronger current price leadership without adding another hardware name. Hold NVDA, AVGO, STX, LITE, DASH, and NFLX: NVDA remains at a fresh high, STX and LITE stabilized above support, and the others remain above their close-based exits. Reconsider SNPS below roughly 545, and reconsider the retained positions on closes below about NVDA 151, AVGO 262, STX 138, LITE 86.5, DASH 232, or NFLX 1215.

journal.text: Hold all seven positions and $1,274.82 cash. Through 2025-07-11, no established close-based exit was breached: NVDA extended to a fresh 164.92 closing high; STX rebounded to 147.18 after holding its breakout area; LITE recovered to 92.99; and AVGO remains in a tight consolidation near its highs. SNPS pulled back modestly to 559.28 after its breakout and remains above the roughly 545 risk level, so reversing the new position after one session is unwarranted. DASH remains above 232. NFLX is the weakest holding after two high-volume declines to 1245.11, but it remains above the 1215 exit and does not yet justify preempting the stated rule. Keep the small cash reserve rather than chase highs. Reconsider on closes below roughly NVDA 151, AVGO 262, STX 138, LITE 86.5, DASH 232, NFLX 1215, or SNPS 545; prioritize an NFLX exit if 1215 breaks or heavy-volume weakness persists.

Hold all seven positions and $1,274.82 cash. Through 2025-07-14, every established close-based risk level remains intact. NVDA held near its record high at 164.07 on lighter volume; STX continued its rebound to 149.08; AVGO remained range-bound near 275.60; and LITE and DASH stayed above support. NFLX rebounded to 1261.95 after two heavy-volume declines, reducing the urgency to exit while it remains above 1215. SNPS is the key risk: it reversed from 579 to 549.53 on exceptional volume and traded below 545 intraday, but its close still held the stated threshold. Honor the close-based rule rather than reacting to one intraday breach, while requiring immediate reassessment if weakness continues. Reconsider on closes below roughly NVDA 151, AVGO 262, STX 138, LITE 86.5, DASH 232, NFLX 1215, or SNPS 545; prioritize selling SNPS on a close below 545 and NFLX below 1215. Keep cash for flexibility rather than chase extended leaders.

Hold all seven positions and $1,274.82 cash. Through 2025-07-15, no close-based exit was breached, while leadership improved: NVDA broke to 170.70 on increased volume, LITE surged to 98.14 on its strongest volume in several sessions, AVGO advanced to 280.94, and SNPS decisively rebounded to 569.10 on elevated volume after the prior reversal. STX held 149.05. DASH weakened to 236.77 but remains above 232, and NFLX consolidated at 1260.27 above 1215; neither warrants preempting the established risk rule. Avoid using the small reserve to chase AMD's high-volume gap or other extended leaders given the portfolio's already heavy technology exposure. Reassess on closes below roughly NVDA 159, AVGO 269, STX 142, LITE 90, DASH 232, NFLX 1215, or SNPS 545; prioritize DASH or NFLX if their thresholds break.

Hold all seven positions and $1,274.82 cash. Through 2025-07-16, no close-based exit was breached. NVDA held its breakout at 171.37, LITE followed its high-volume surge with a further gain to 99.63, and AVGO stayed near its highs at 280.81. STX eased to 147.12 but remains above 142. DASH is the closest risk, declining a second day to 234.50, yet it still closed above 232; honor the established rule rather than sell just before confirmation. NFLX remains weak at 1250.31 but above 1215. SNPS closed higher at 571.20 despite an unusually wide, very high-volume session, warranting monitoring rather than an exit while 545 holds. Do not deploy the small reserve into AMD after its sharp two-day run, especially given heavy existing semiconductor exposure. Reassess on closes below roughly NVDA 159, AVGO 269, STX 142, LITE 90, DASH 232, NFLX 1215, or SNPS 545; prioritize DASH if 232 breaks and remain alert to SNPS follow-through after the volume spike.

Hold all seven positions and $1,274.82 cash. Through 2025-07-17, every close-based risk threshold remains intact. NVDA extended to 173, AVGO broke higher to 286.45, and LITE reached 102.64 on renewed volume, so their momentum argues against trimming winners. SNPS also followed its volatile high-volume rebound with a strong close at 589.01. DASH remains the nearest risk: it tested 232.10 intraday but recovered to 235.02, still above the established 232 closing trigger. NFLX rebounded to 1274.17 on unusually heavy volume, while STX held 146.72 despite elevated turnover. Do not chase strength with the small reserve given concentrated technology exposure. Reassess on closes below roughly NVDA 159, AVGO 269, STX 142, LITE 94, DASH 232, NFLX 1215, or SNPS 550; prioritize DASH if 232 breaks and watch STX for confirmation below 142.

Exit the full NFLX position, then rotate $6,000 into GOOG. NFLX closed at 1209.24, below the established 1215 risk trigger, after a sharp reversal on 10.69 million shares; honoring the close-based rule takes priority over hoping for a rebound. GOOG offers a steadier replacement outside the portfolio's semiconductor cluster: it advanced from 175.16 on July 8 to 185.94 on July 18 and cleared its June/early-July resistance around 181-185 without a one-day vertical surge. Retain the residual cash and hold NVDA, AVGO, STX, LITE, DASH, and SNPS, whose prior closing thresholds remain intact. Reassess GOOG on a close below roughly 179, and the other positions below approximately NVDA 159, AVGO 269, STX 142, LITE 94, DASH 232, or SNPS 550.

Hold all seven positions and $1,583.16 cash. Through 2025-07-21, every close-based risk threshold remains intact. GOOG validated yesterday's rotation by advancing to 191.15 on stronger volume and closing near its high, but the 2.8% one-day move argues against immediately chasing with the small reserve. AVGO closed at 288.21 near a new high, LITE reached 103.84 on increased volume, and SNPS advanced to 591.46; their trends remain constructive. NVDA's mild two-day pullback to 171.38 came on declining volume and remains well above support. STX held 149.63, while DASH's recovery to 240.53 creates welcome distance from its risk level. Preserve the modest 3.1% cash buffer rather than deepen already substantial technology exposure. Reassess on closes below roughly GOOG 179, NVDA 159, AVGO 269, STX 142, LITE 94, DASH 232, or SNPS 550.

Hold all seven positions and $1,583.16 cash. The July 22 semiconductor/AI pullback warrants attention but not a reaction before support breaks: NVDA closed 167.03 after testing 164.58, AVGO 278.59 after testing 276.43, LITE 99.63, and STX 146.59; each remains above its established closing risk level. DASH held 239.82 on light volume, GOOG consolidated constructively at 192.11 after its breakout, and SNPS accelerated to a 615.13 high close, offsetting some weakness. With only a 3.1% reserve and substantial technology exposure, neither chase SNPS nor add into a one-day decline. Reassess on closes below roughly GOOG 179, NVDA 159, AVGO 269, STX 142, LITE 94, DASH 232, or SNPS 575; also treat another heavy-volume NVDA/LITE decline as confirmation of deteriorating momentum.

Hold all seven positions and $1,583.16 cash. The July 23 action repaired the prior session's weakness: NVDA rebounded to 170.78, AVGO to 283.69, LITE to 102.13, and STX surged to a 152.76 closing high on improved volume. SNPS held its sharp breakout at 614.42, while GOOG's 191.51 consolidation and DASH's 240.56 close remain above support. No close-based exit is triggered, and the small 3.1% reserve does not justify chasing strength or adding further technology concentration. Reassess on closes below approximately GOOG 179, NVDA 159, AVGO 269, STX 142, LITE 94, DASH 232, or SNPS 575; a renewed heavy-volume reversal would also warrant reducing risk.

Hold all seven positions and $1,583.16 cash. July 24 preserved the portfolio's constructive trend: NVDA closed at a fresh 30-session high of 173.74, AVGO recovered to 288.71, STX held its breakout at 152.73, and LITE consolidated at 102.85 on light volume. DASH improved to 243.69, while SNPS's orderly pullback to 609.68 remains well above support. GOOG's earnings-like gap to 198.11 faded on heavy volume, but the 193.20 close still held above the prior breakout area, so it is a caution signal rather than an exit. With every position above its close-based risk level and only a 3.1% cash reserve, avoid unnecessary turnover or chasing. Reassess on closes below approximately GOOG 187, NVDA 164, AVGO 276, STX 146, LITE 97, DASH 232, or SNPS 575; reduce sooner if GOOG's high-volume fade receives downside follow-through or weakness broadens across multiple holdings.

Hold all seven positions and $1,583.16 cash. July 25 remained constructive: NVDA held near its new high at 173.50, AVGO advanced to 290.18, LITE reached a new 40-session closing high at 104.52, and DASH broke above its prior range to 249.92 on improved volume. STX's pullback to 150.89 stayed above breakout support, while GOOG stabilized at 194.08 after the prior high-volume gap fade. SNPS declined for a third session to 601.55, but remains above its breakout/support zone and does not yet justify turnover. With all holdings above risk levels and cash only 3.1% of account value, preserve the reserve rather than chase fresh highs. Reassess on closes below roughly GOOG 187, NVDA 164, AVGO 276, STX 146, LITE 97, DASH 239, or SNPS 575; SNPS weakness below 590 or broad downside across the momentum holdings would warrant earlier risk reduction.

Hold all seven positions and $1,583.16 cash. July 28 kept the main momentum trends intact: NVDA closed at a new high of 176.75, AVGO at 294.30, and LITE at 107.17. STX consolidated at 150.46 above breakout support, while GOOG held 193.42 after its recent high-volume gap fade and DASH's pullback to 246.44 stayed above its breakout area. SNPS weakened for a fourth session to 592.63 and briefly traded below 590, but recovered above that level and remains above more important support near 575; it is the position requiring closest monitoring. With no close-based exit triggered and cash only 3.1% of account value, avoid turnover or chasing extended leaders. Reassess on closes below roughly GOOG 187, NVDA 167, AVGO 280, STX 146, LITE 100, DASH 239, or SNPS 575; continued SNPS weakness below 590 or broad downside across holdings would justify reducing risk.

Hold all seven positions and $1,583.16 cash. July 29 was broadly constructive: AVGO advanced to a new closing high at 297.42, LITE extended its breakout to 109.48, GOOG strengthened to 196.43, and SNPS reversed its four-session pullback with a high-volume gap to 635.81 and a fresh high. NVDA eased to 175.51 after reaching 179.38 but remains near its peak. STX closed up at 152.68 on elevated volume despite fading from 155.52, while DASH weakened for a second day to 243.20 but still held above the 239 breakout/support area. No close-based exit has triggered, and the small 3.0% cash reserve is not enough to improve the portfolio materially without selling a still-valid trend. Reassess on closes below roughly NVDA 167, AVGO 284, STX 146, LITE 102, DASH 239, SNPS 600, or GOOG 190; DASH below 239 or failed follow-through in SNPS after its gap would justify reducing risk.

Hold all seven positions and $1,583.16 cash. July 30 strengthened most of the portfolio: NVDA, AVGO, SNPS, and GOOG closed at fresh highs, LITE consolidated near its breakout high, and DASH rebounded from 243.20 to 248.00. STX was the exception, gapping down to 141 and trading as low as 138.30 on very heavy volume, but its recovery to 147.42 preserved the prior 146 closing-support area; that reversal argues against selling at the next open, though STX now requires close monitoring. With six trends clearly constructive and STX still above its close-based exit, avoid unnecessary turnover ahead of the next scheduled monthly funding. Reassess on closes below roughly NVDA 170, AVGO 290, STX 146 (especially renewed weakness toward 140), LITE 103, DASH 239, SNPS 615, or GOOG 190.

Deploy $35,000 of the new monthly cash into five relative-strength leaders while retaining about $16,583 cash for volatility. Buy META after its high-volume gap to a record close; ALNY after a decisive high-volume breakout from the 310-345 range; CEG after a two-day breakout to new highs; APP after its high-volume gap/reclaim of the recent range; and INSM as it resumes its longer uptrend at a fresh closing high. The mix broadens the existing portfolio across mega-cap technology, application software, power, and biotechnology. Hold all seven prior positions: STX's powerful rebound to 157.01 confirms the July 30 reversal, while NVDA, LITE, DASH, SNPS, GOOG and AVGO remain constructive despite July 31's broader intraday reversals. Reconsider new positions on closes below roughly META 735, ALNY 350, CEG 328, APP 360, or INSM 101. For existing holdings, monitor NVDA 170, AVGO 284-290, STX 146, LITE 103, DASH 239, SNPS 615, and GOOG 190; broad failure of these levels would favor raising cash.

journal.text: Hold all 12 positions and $16,583.16 cash. The August 1 risk-off session did not produce a decisive close-based exit: NVDA held 173.72 above 170, AVGO closed 288.64 within its 284-290 support zone, STX held 154.81 above 146, LITE recovered from 101.61 to 106.68 above 103, DASH held 248.35 above 239, and SNPS held 618.65 above 615. GOOG finished essentially at its 190 level (189.95), so it warrants close monitoring rather than a sale on a five-cent breach. Friday's new positions were also constructive overall: ALNY extended to a record 401.80, INSM reached a fresh closing high at 108.69, while META, CEG, and APP remained above their stated 735, 328, and 360 risk levels. Preserve the 16.2% cash reserve after the broad reversal instead of chasing strength or reacting to one marginal support test. Reconsider on closes below GOOG 188-190, NVDA 170, AVGO 284, STX 146, LITE 103, DASH 239, SNPS 615, META 735, ALNY 382 (with 350 as major support), CEG 328, APP 360, or INSM 101; multiple breaches would favor materially raising cash.

Hold all 12 positions and $16,583.16 cash. The August 4 rebound repaired Friday's broad weakness without creating a compelling need to chase at an unknown opening price: NVDA reclaimed 180, AVGO 297.72, LITE 111.13, DASH broke to 258.02, GOOG recovered to 195.75, and META returned to 776.37. ALNY, CEG, APP, and INSM all extended their relative-strength trends, while SNPS rebounded above 636 and STX held 154.81. No position breached its close-based risk level. Keep the 15.8% cash reserve because the recovery is only one session old and the portfolio is already broadly invested across 12 names; screened alternatives were either extended after gaps or offered no clear upgrade over current holdings. Reconsider on closes below NVDA 170, AVGO 284, STX 146, LITE 103, DASH 239-243, SNPS 615, GOOG 188-190, META 735, ALNY 398 then 382, CEG 328, APP 360, or INSM 101-103. Multiple breaches would favor raising cash; orderly consolidation or fresh breakouts could justify deploying part of the reserve.

Deploy $5,000 of the cash reserve into PLTR after its high-volume gap to a record close: it opened at 171.81, reached 176.33, and held 173.27 on 130.9 million shares, a cleaner fresh breakout than the mostly extended or weakening alternatives. Retain roughly $11,583 cash and hold all 12 existing positions. August 5 was a broad pullback, but none of the close-based risk levels failed; INSM and ALNY remained near highs, GOOG held 195, and NVDA, AVGO, STX, LITE, DASH, SNPS, META, CEG, and APP stayed above support despite reversals. Reconsider PLTR on a close below roughly 160-164, especially if the earnings-gap area fails. Existing risk levels remain NVDA 170, AVGO 284, STX 146, LITE 103, DASH 239-243, SNPS 615, GOOG 188-190, META 735, ALNY 398 then 382, CEG 328, APP 360, and INSM 101-103; multiple breaches would favor raising cash rather than adding further exposure.

journal.text: Hold all 13 positions and $11,583.16 cash. Reconsider promptly on closes below STX 146, CEG 328, SNPS 615, PLTR 164-170, NVDA 170, AVGO 284, LITE 103, DASH 243, GOOG 188-190, META 735, APP 360, INSM 103, or ALNY 398; multiple failures would favor raising cash.

Hold all 13 positions and $11,583.16 cash. August 7 strengthened the portfolio's leadership: APP broke out on 20.7 million shares to 437.34, DASH gapped to 270.99 on 10.9 million shares, and PLTR and ALNY advanced to fresh highs at 182.20 and 435.10. NVDA, AVGO, GOOG, LITE, and INSM remain constructive. The weaker holdings still met close-based discipline: STX recovered from 144.75 to close 148.10 above 146; CEG rebounded from 322 to 336.41 above 328; and SNPS closed 620.33 above 615. With several holdings already extended after gaps, retain the 10.9% reserve rather than chase AAPL, SHOP, AXON, WMT, or other recent surges at an unknown open. Reconsider on closes below STX 146, CEG 328, SNPS 615, PLTR 170 (more serious below 164), NVDA 170, AVGO 284, LITE 103, DASH 258 then 243, GOOG 188-190, META 735, APP 390 then 360, INSM 103, or ALNY 398; multiple failures would favor raising cash.

Buy $5,000 of CSCO and retain roughly $6,583 cash, while holding all 13 existing positions. CSCO closed at 71.79 after clearing its prior 100-session high on 31.7 million shares; the three-day advance from 67.52 is orderly and offers a less extended new position than the sharp AAPL, APP, PLTR, or GILD moves. Existing leadership remains strong: LITE made a high-volume record close at 116.27, GOOG cleared 200, NVDA neared its high, and PLTR, APP, and ALNY held record territory. DASH reversed its earnings gap but closed 259.19 just above the precommitted 258 level, so hold but watch closely. Reconsider CSCO below 69, and exit more decisively below 67.5. Existing close-based risk levels remain DASH 258 then 243, STX 146, CEG 328, SNPS 615, PLTR 170, NVDA 170, AVGO 284, LITE 103, GOOG 190, META 735, APP 390 then 360, INSM 103, and ALNY 398; multiple failures would favor raising cash.

Exit the full DASH position after its 256.09 close breached the precommitted 258 risk level; the earnings gap has now faded for two sessions, with an August 11 low of 251.13, so discipline outweighs its still-positive longer trend. Rotate $5,000 into WMT. WMT broke above its July range on August 6 with a 103.36 close and 23.7 million shares, then held the breakout tightly for three sessions, closing 103.93 on August 11; this adds steadier non-tech leadership while retaining an estimated $8,800 cash reserve after the DASH sale. Hold the other 13 positions: APP, ALNY, GOOG, NVDA, PLTR, INSM, STX and LITE remain strong, while CEG and SNPS are close to risk levels and CSCO is testing its new breakout. Reconsider WMT below 101, more decisively below 99; existing close-based levels remain CSCO 69 then 67.5, CEG 328, SNPS 615, STX 146, PLTR/NVDA 170, AVGO 284, LITE 103, GOOG 190, META 735, APP 390, INSM 103, and ALNY 398.

Hold all 14 positions and $8,881.40 cash. August 12 improved rather than impaired the setup: LITE closed at a record 119.66 on 5.86 million shares, INSM broke decisively to 122 on 7.25 million shares, AVGO reached a new high at 312.83, and META, GOOG, APP, PLTR, NVDA, and STX all remained constructive. CEG rebounded to 338.57 and SNPS recovered to 625.80, keeping both above their precommitted 328 and 615 risk levels; CSCO also held its breakout area at 71.38. WMT's 103.62 close continues to hold the August 6 breakout, so one quiet session after purchase does not warrant reversal. With leadership already represented and fresh candidates such as MU extended after sharp multi-day runs, retain the 8.2% reserve rather than chase at an unknown open. Reconsider on closes below WMT 101, CSCO 69 then 67.5, CEG 328, SNPS 615, STX 146, PLTR/NVDA 170, AVGO 284, LITE 110 then 103, GOOG 190, META 735, APP 430 then 390, INSM 112 then 103, and ALNY 398; multiple simultaneous failures would favor raising cash.

Exit CEG and WMT in full and hold the remaining 12 positions, raising cash to roughly 19% before any opening gaps. CEG closed at 327.63, breaching the precommitted 328 risk level after falling from a 342.75 intraday high to near the low on increased volume; its rebound has failed and discipline requires the sale. WMT closed at 100.99, effectively below the precommitted 101 level, after gapping down and finishing near its 100.85 low on 19.4 million shares; the August 6 breakout has failed, so reverse the recent purchase promptly. Do not redeploy immediately because August 13 also brought notable reversals in APP and LITE and softer closes across several leaders. Retain CSCO while above 69 and SNPS while above 615; other key close-based levels remain STX 146, PLTR/NVDA 170, AVGO 284, LITE 110 then 103, GOOG 190, META 735, APP 430 then 390, INSM 112 then 103, and ALNY 398. Reconsider deploying cash after leaders stabilize or produce fresh breakouts; further simultaneous support failures would favor additional defense.

Hold all 12 positions and $20,507.32 cash. The August 14 close did not trigger any precommitted exit: CSCO recovered from a 67.48 intraday low to 69.30 despite heavy volume, narrowly retaining 69; SNPS held 615 at 616.36; APP held 430 at 433.34; and LITE held 110 at 114.62. The latter two remain under pressure after sharp reversals, so the roughly 19% cash reserve is preferable to chasing fresh strength. INSM advanced to a new 127.75 high on elevated volume, ALNY closed near its high at 442.73, and AVGO, NVDA, GOOG, META, STX and PLTR remain above support. Do not add despite notable momentum in INTC and improving semiconductors because several current leaders are testing nearby risk levels. Reconsider on closes below CSCO 69 (more decisively 67.5), SNPS 615, APP 430 then 390, LITE 110 then 103, STX 146, PLTR/NVDA 170, AVGO 284, GOOG 190, META 735, INSM 112 then 103, and ALNY 398; deploy cash only after leaders stabilize or fresh breakouts hold.

Sell CSCO in full and retain the other 11 positions. CSCO closed August 15 at 66.20, decisively below both the 69 and 67.5 precommitted risk levels, after trading down to 65.86 and finishing near the low on 40.9 million shares. The attempted post-earnings recovery has failed, so exit rather than widen the stop; the sale should lift cash to roughly 23% before any opening gap. Do not redeploy today: semiconductor weakness broadened sharply in AMAT, KLAC and LRCX, PLTR has retreated to 177.17, and SNPS remains only marginally above 615. Current holdings otherwise retained support, with APP recovering to 438.68, LITE to 115.86, and INSM and ALNY near highs. Reconsider on closes below SNPS 615, APP 430 then 390, LITE 110 then 103, STX 146, PLTR/NVDA 170, AVGO 284, GOOG 190, META 735, INSM 112 then 103, and ALNY 420 then 398. Deploy cash only after market leadership stabilizes or a fresh breakout proves durable.
